h.select_rule: Keep hypotheses whose direction goes against the first intuitive guess but which a reported empirical regularity or a general statistical effect (headroom, floor, saturation, redundancy) supports. Drop those with rare conditions or tiny expected effects. Keep variety across edited fields.
h.strategy: Use the retrieved literature to find measured interaction patterns, not design advice: reports that an option's benefit shrinks, vanishes or reverses depending on what else is present, or that strong configurations respond differently from weak ones. Translate each reported pattern into a conditional hypothesis about this benchmark. Write queries about interactions, diminishing returns and context-dependent effects among components. Include hypotheses in which strong parents gain less from improvements and lose more from degradations. Choose conditions that many parents satisfy.

hyps.why: A cell that already has a strong conv on edge 5 gains less from another conv (diminishing returns).
A strong parent on edge 0 leaves less headroom for the added conv.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 is dead and edge 2 contributes nothing, so the edit has little effect.
With node 1 disconnected from the input, a conv on edge 4 has little effect.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, all signal goes through node 1, so the edge 0 conv matters more.
With no direct path, the final hop conv carries more of the representation.
Adding a direct skip path where none existed improves gradient flow more than replacing other ops with skip.
Removing a skip shortcut hurts more than removing weak ops.
Adding any parametric op to an empty edge gives a larger gain than replacing a non-empty op.
Adding a direct input-to-output conv path where none existed gives a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
